style: Quiet, clean, close to skin. Scent should not reach the next person on a crowded train.
roots: Kōdō, the art of 'listening' to incense, dates back about a thousand years. Many perfumes borrow agarwood, hinoki, yuzu, green tea and seasonal flowers.

style: Soft 'skin scents', herbal and musky, sold in design-led stores. Moving from sweet florals to woods and tobacco.
roots: Seoul's design scene turned perfume into a lifestyle and gallery experience.

style: The new 'Eastern aesthetic' wave: tea, osmanthus, magnolia, incense, ink, moss gardens, poetry.
roots: Chinese incense and herbal culture, reworked by young houses since about 2018; big brands are now investing.
where: Shanghai and Beijing flagship stores; Tmall/Taobao online

style: Tiny indie scene with temple, tea and hometown-flower stories.
roots: Temple incense and oolong tea culture.

style: Two worlds: alcohol-free attars and ruhs from Kannauj and Delhi, and new modern houses telling city stories.
roots: Kannauj has distilled flowers into sandalwood oil for centuries; 'mitti' attar even captures the smell of first rain on earth.
where: Chandni Chowk (Delhi), Kannauj, online craft stores

style: Spice-garden and temple-flower scents tied to Ayurveda.
roots: Cinnamon is native to Sri Lanka; temple offerings of lotus and jasmine.

style: Apothecary oils, balms and solid perfumes; new Bangkok houses (textile-themed, dessert-themed, place-themed) built to last in tropical heat.
roots: Thai-Chinese herbal apothecaries, jasmine garlands, and yadom: small herbal inhalers and balms (camphor, menthol, borneol) that travellers bring home as souvenirs.
where: Bangkok: CentralWorld, ICONSIAM, Karmakamet Scentorium, Beautrium and Watsons

style: Fast-growing local brands with bold, long-lasting scents.
roots: Indonesia supplies much of the world's patchouli, vetiver, clove and nutmeg.

style: Proudly local: sampaguita, calamansi, dalandan, coffee, sea salt, and place-based stories.
roots: Sampaguita is the national flower, strung into garlands.
where: Manila; Instagram shops; TADHANA ships from Canada

style: Newly forming scene with city portraits, coffee and tea themes.
roots: Coffee culture, lotus, incense and rice.

style: Grand, layered luxury built on frankincense.
roots: Oman's Dhofar region has traded frankincense for thousands of years.

style: Oud oils, bakhoor and heavy oil blends; scent is layered on skin, hair, clothes and rooms.
roots: Arabian hospitality and incense-burning traditions.

style: Rich, sweet, very long-lasting; the source of today's online 'Arabian perfume' trend and many close alternatives to designer scents.
roots: Gulf trading hub mixing Indian, Persian and Arab traditions.

style: Ottoman stories in strong extrait concentrations.
roots: Ottoman rose water, spice markets and coffee houses.

style: Natural small-batch perfumes using indigenous plants, plus an affordable inspired-by market.
roots: The Cape's fynbos plants, like buchu, used in traditional medicine.

style: Strong, projecting scents in big 100 ml bottles; growing local houses.
roots: A large, perfume-loving market long supplied by imports and Gulf brands.

style: Native-plant perfumery: copal, vanilla, tobacco, agave, citrus blossom.
roots: Copal has been burned in ceremonies since Maya times; vanilla is native to Mexico.

style: Botanical-expedition perfumery with Patagonian and Amazonian plants.
roots: South American flora and clean-formula craft.

style: Big local beauty brands with Amazon ingredients and fresh, green scents.
roots: Amazon biodiversity and community sourcing.

style: Small, art-driven indie houses.
roots: Toronto indie perfume community.

style: Story-driven indie perfumery, often with playful concepts.
roots: Portland and Brooklyn indie scenes.

style: Native Australian botanicals and coastal moods.
roots: Indigenous plants like Australian sandalwood, desert lime and coastal moss.

style: Small natural perfumers and cult niche projects.
roots: Amsterdam's independent scene.

style: Sweet, rich Gulf taste, increasingly in light body sprays as well as oud and oils.
roots: Gulf incense and oil traditions; a strong local fashion-and-beauty scene online.

style: Drugstore hair and body mists with dessert and fruit scents; very price-driven.
roots: Rossmann and Hebe drugstore culture.

style: Designer houses that act like niche, with unusual material pairings.
roots: Antwerp fashion.

style: A trading-port mix: Malay, Arab, Indian and Chinese scent traditions, from attar shops to modern home-scent brands.
roots: Kampong Glam's Arab Street has sold attars and oils for generations.

style: Small studios inspired by coast, bush and Māori plant knowledge.
roots: Rongoā Māori (traditional plant healing) and wild coastlines.

style: The home of modern perfumery: Grasse grows the flowers, Paris houses range from quiet, nature-first (Diptyque, Goutal) to bold and provocative.
roots: Grasse has supplied jasmine, rose and tuberose since the 1600s; Paris turned perfume into fashion.
where: Paris: Saint-Germain, Le Marais, Galeries Lafayette; Grasse

style: English gardens, tea and gentle florals, plus Victorian heritage houses.
roots: London perfumers to the royal court since the 1800s.
where: London: Covent Garden, Mayfair, Burlington Arcade

style: From ancient monastery colognes to bold luxury extraits.
roots: Florentine pharmacies and the Renaissance cologne tradition; Calabrian bergamot.

style: Minimal, memory-based, genderless scents.
roots: Scandinavian design.

style: Nordic landscapes and essential-oil-led blends.
roots: Hygge and Nordic nature.

style: Precise, clean woods and musks from master perfumers.
roots: Geneva is home to big fragrance companies (Firmenich, Givaudan).

style: Heritage soaps and colognes with Art Deco packaging.
roots: Porto soap-making since the 1800s.

style: Sunny Aegean scents: figs, beach, herbs.
roots: Mediterranean herbs and pharmacy tradition.

style: Small Berlin perfumeries and city-themed scents.
roots: Berlin's linden-lined streets and 1920s perfume history.

style: Warm, passionate Mediterranean scents and fragrance dynasties.
roots: Barcelona's perfume families.

style: Orange blossom, rose and jasmine from the countryside, plus rich musks and spices from the souks.
roots: Rose valley near Kelaat M'Gouna, orange blossom water traditions and Berber harvesting.

style: Bohemian apothecary scents built on spices, herbs and Mediterranean citrus.
roots: Jaffa's old port and spice trade.

style: Tiny natural-perfume ateliers specialising in rare oud and resins.
roots: An artisan community focused on natural distillations.

style: Source of some of the world's most prized wild agarwood (oud).
roots: Agarwood forests of Southeast Asia.

style: A small, personal scene of indie perfumers who bottle wet Irish landscapes: moss, fern, gorse, wool, rain, sea air and church incense, usually soft and natural rather than loud.
roots: No old perfume industry, but a strong smell culture: turf fires, coconut-scented gorse on the hills, the Atlantic coast. Today's perfume houses grew up in the west of Ireland, in the Burren and Galway.
where: Dublin: Parfumarija (Westbury Mall), Cloon Keen (Powerscourt Townhouse), Brown Thomas on Grafton Street; Galway High Street; the Burren in County Clare

style: Old perfume roots and a lively everyday scene: perfume-oil shops that blend to order, sweet musky body scents, oud and bakhoor, and big shareable bottles sold through Instagram.
roots: Ancient Egypt burned resins and blended scented oils (see kyphi). Egypt is still a major grower of jasmine for the perfume industry.
where: Cairo's old perfume-oil shops around Khan el-Khalili; small brands sell through Instagram
